verdict.rationale: Sandbox0 documents first-party pause and resume of the same sandbox, preserving the writable root filesystem across checkpoints. Paused sandboxes incur storage charges only, and auto-resume and soft-TTL-driven pause are also documented. Memory preservation is only an experimental opt-in (`memory: true`) that covers "supported process state", so the memory half of the story carries documented limitations. Missing for 10: memory pause/resume beyond experimental status with all process state supported, and independent or hands-on corroboration of state surviving a resume.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause a running sandbox and resume it later with filesystem and memory state intact

citations.quote: Preserve the whole writable root filesystem across successful checkpoints, pause compute between tasks, and resume the same sandbox when work returns.
Experimental memory pause/resume explicitly opts into preserving supported process state with `memory: true`.
Incremental RootFS · retained memory · shared data counted once
With auto_resume enabled, supported inbound access can wake a paused sandbox; resume takes time and requires available capacity.
